newsitem.title: USA: House panel clarifies bank muni underwriting plan.
newsitem.headline: House panel clarifies bank muni underwriting plan.

text.p: The House Banking Committee voted on Tuesday to clear up a technical glitch in bank modernization legislation that would have required national banks to register with the SEC before underwriting muni revenue bonds.
The committee is debating a bill to comprehensively overhaul U.S. banking laws and allow banks to freely enter other financial sectors like insurance and securities underwriting.
One provision would permit banks to directly underwrite municipal revenue bonds without first setting up a separate subsidiary.
A related provision would have required banks that want to underwrite muni revenue bonds to register the securities first with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Sarah Miller, senior government relations counsel for the American Bankers Association, said earlier Tuesday that the registration language was added due to a clerical "oversight" and that it would be stripped out of the bill.

As Miller forecast, the committee approved a block of technical amendments that would drop the SEC registration requirement. Debate on the bill by the committee chaired by Iowa Republican James Leach is expected to resume Wednesday.
